title: Double-Negative Maze
blurb: A robot crosses a maze, and at every junction a tricky instruction full of negatives says which way to go. A wrong turn hits a wall.
lesson: Negatives and indirection are on Jev's known-weakness list, so watch its confidence: when it drops, rewrite the instruction plainly or send the case to a person.
why: TypeSafe lists literal reading, double negatives and multi-hop wording among Jev 1.13's weak spots. Every junction here is one of them, written so it has exactly one right answer.

Jev's confidence comes with every Choice, so a low number marks the instructions it found hard. An LLM that writes out its reasoning instead of the answer format counts as a miss, and its raw output is shown in the list below.
